newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian industry leader Fossa favours mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian industry leader Fossa favours mini-budget.

text.p: Giorgio Fossa, the President of Italy's industrialists' association Confindustria said on Friday that bringing forward the 1998 budget should not be an excuse to rule out a mini-budget.
"An early 1998 budget would be a strong and good signal to the markets," Fossa told Italian weekly Il Mondo. A transcript of the interview was made available ahead of publication.
"But I would not like the passage of the 1998 budget to be brought forward while not carrying through a mini-budget," Fossa added.
The Italian budget must be drawn up by September 30 and has to be passed into law by the end of December.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he could not rule out a "modest" mini-budget and said he would still like to bring forward the full 1998 budget but would need clear backing in parliament to do so.
Prodi told a news conference after a cabinet meeting that he did not exclude a mini-budget for this year of "modest size".
